candidates.name: LIDAR Vegetation Object Model (VOM)
verified_facts: The Vegetation Object Model is a derived raster based on National LIDAR Programme 1m elevation data plus GIS modelling and other mapping/imagery inputs.
Its pixels represent canopy height above ground for classified vegetation and the record warns of potential misclassifications and limited manual quality control.
semantic_limits: Derived canopy-height modelling is not a bare-earth terrain observation and must not be substituted for DTM parcel elevation or used to raise ground-height confidence.

candidates.name: Accuracy of OS Net, OSTN15 and OSGM15
verified_facts: OS reports OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors generally better than 0.008m in plan and 0.020m in height.
For Great Britain OSGM15 height standard error is stated as 0.008m, explicitly excluding GNSS heighting errors; OSTN15 transformation statements similarly exclude source GNSS positional errors.
semantic_limits: Transformation-model or control-network accuracy cannot be used as the complete parcel-height uncertainty; GNSS, source raster, geometry, sampling and survey errors remain separate components.
